confidence_notes: Restaurant meals, coffee and beer are fairly well supported by the searches. They mainly turned up Numbeo-derived figures reported by Expatica for June 2026, plus MyLifeElsewhere and other budget sites. Those figures were reported in euros: inexpensive meal about €19, three-course meal for two about €52, 0.5 L draught beer about €3.1, cappuccino about €2.1. I converted them to USD using an assumed EUR/USD of roughly 1.15, which I did not look up, and nudged beer up for restaurant serving prices. The searches found no reliable current price for cocktails or wine by the glass. I estimated both from the local beer price and general knowledge of Spanish bar prices: cocktail about €10-11, wine about €4. Accommodation was not searched. Those four anchors are holistic model estimates, set for July peak season, when San Sebastian is among Spain's priciest cities. They carry the most uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: Basis is San Sebastian's own aggregated price indexes, which show it about 15% above the Spanish average. Accommodation is benchmarked loosely against other high-demand Spanish and Basque coastal destinations in peak summer.
